findings.text: Dirty tracking entries use two low flag bits, one meaning dirty and one meaning reset requested, with a two bit mask covering both.
A dirty frame descriptor holds a flags word and slot identifier followed by a wide offset of the page inside the slot.
Bus lock detection offers off and exit mode selectors in low bits, and performance monitoring capability offers a disable selector in the lowest bit.
Statistics file header is six narrow words describing flags, name length, descriptor count, and byte positions of identity, descriptors and values.

Statistic descriptor flags pack a low nibble type, a middle nibble unit and a higher nibble numeric base, each with shift, mask, enumerated values and a maximum sentinel covering cumulative through log histogram, none through boolean, and decimal through binary power.
Each statistic descriptor holds flags, signed exponent, element size, value offset and histogram bucket width followed by a name field that is fixed size in kernel and flexible elsewhere.
Fixed selectors identify statistics file retrieval, extended save state retrieval, S390 protected virtualization CPU command and S390 PCI operation.

Memory attribute control is a quadruple of wide words for address, size, attributes and flags; guest file creation is size, flags plus reserved words; pre-fault is guest address, size, flags plus padding.
Private memory is a single upper attribute bit, guest file creation offers mapping and initial shared mode bits, and three operations select attribute setting, guest file creation and pre-fault.
x86 notification exit control exposes enabled and user delivery selectors in the two lowest positions of a wide mask.

Paravirtual layer defines a distinct unimplemented number plus fault, invalid, too large, permission and unsupported mappings, and host call numbers one through twelve for polling, memory management, features, magic page, kick, clock query, exit, console, clock pairing, IPI, yield and range mapping.
Per virtual CPU async fault state is prepared by emptying completed and queued lists and initializing its dedicated lock, with a build without the feature providing an empty operation.

Background fault completion tries to make the faulting host address present while the owning process still exists, notifies architecture code either immediately or only when the first completion is queued depending on build, appends to the completed list under protection, records completion and wakes the CPU even on failure so synchronous retry can proceed.

Statistics streaming exposes one linear byte view formed by header, fixed identity string, descriptor array and value area, honors caller offset and remaining length, advances the offset, ends with zero at end of data, and reports a memory fault if delivery to user fails.
Coalesced device wrapper links list membership, generic device hooks, owning machine pointer and a zone descriptor with address, size and port versus memory selector.
A coalesced access is accepted only for non-negative length without address wrap and fully contained inside the configured zone bounds.

Coalesced writes serialize on the machine ring lock, reject out of range or out of bounds producer positions and a nearly full ring that keeps one slot free to separate empty from full, then store address, length, payload and port marker with ordering before publishing the advanced producer index.

Coalesced support starts on a zeroed shared page with lock and zone list initialization, registers zones only for port selectors zero or one on the matching bus while holding the slot mutex with cleanup on failure, and unregisters every zone containing the requested range while holding the same mutex while always reporting success.

Dirty ring allocation reserves zeroed storage sized by entry count, derives capacity from byte size, subtracts fixed plus architecture reserved entries to form a soft limit, and clears producer and reset positions with an index tag.
Machine memory management protection has two build variants for acquire and release around the machine lock, one write oriented and one spin based, used when enabling dirty logging for a batch.

Single batch dirty reset decodes the slot handle into address space and index parts, ignores unknown spaces, slots, offsets or masks reaching past the slot page count, and otherwise enables logging for the masked pages under memory management protection.

Dirty entries move from active to harvested when a consumer marks reset requested as seen with acquire semantics, then to invalid by clearing flags with release semantics during reset; reset needs the slot mutex, stops at the first non-harvested entry, coalesces nearby offsets in one slot into a mask with forward and constrained backward merging while yielding, aborts on pending signals, flushes a final batch and records a trace.
Dirty ring page lookup translates a page granular offset into the host page backing the virtually allocated ring storage.

Interrupt file descriptors inject through distinct source identities, with simple descriptors asserting then deasserting while resample descriptors assert only and deassert on acknowledgement before notifying waiters under read side protection; shutdown waits for initialization, detaches wait queues, drains pending injection, tears down resample membership freeing the final member and unregistering its notifier, then releases references.

Resample list changes serialize on a dedicated mutex with expedited read side synchronization on removal, traversal uses sleepable read side sections, and coalesced and async completion paths serialize on the machine ring lock and per CPU lock respectively.

Racing consumers can set the coalesced producer index out of range, continuously re-dirty rings during reset, or trigger delivery faults and signal interruption; handling bounds checks the index, keeps one ring slot free, orders publication, returns fault status on copy failure and aborts reset on signals.
Machine level services in this lane expose coalesced zone management, dirty ring allocation reset and page lookup, statistics streaming, and per CPU async fault preparation.
Headers use include guards against multiple inclusion, and the coalesced header supplies a no operation initializer reporting success when disabled.
Async fault handling retains a dedicated cache pointer for request objects and interrupt descriptor handling retains a dedicated cleanup workqueue pointer.
Architecture permission hook for interrupt descriptors defaults to approval for all requests.
